features.name: Production CSS inlining
features.summary: Inlining puts the page's CSS in a <style> tag in the HTML instead of linking a stylesheet.
features.whatHtml: Inlining puts the page's CSS in a <style> tag in the HTML instead of linking a stylesheet. In principle that removes one render-blocking stylesheet request from the critical path; frameworks without it (Waku, Ember) still link the built stylesheet.
features.gotchasHtml:
• Nuxt keeps inlineStyles off in dev so stylesheet HMR still works; check the production build.
  • A ?inline import puts the whole stylesheet in every HTML response, so it only suits small stylesheets.

features.name: Font optimization
features.summary: A web font is discovered late: the browser finds it only after the CSS that names it has loaded.
features.whatHtml: A web font is discovered late: the browser finds it only after the CSS that names it has loaded. Font optimization self-hosts the files, generates the @font-face rules, and can preload the file. In principle, self-hosting the font (via either route) removes a cross-origin request from the critical path.
features.gotchasHtml:
• Of the frameworks in the main tables, only Next, Nuxt (the official @nuxt/fonts module), and Pracht have a first-party font feature. Next uses it here; the Nuxt and Pracht ports use Fontsource instead.
  • Importing Fontsource alone does not preload anything. Without a <link rel="preload"> the browser finds the font only after the stylesheet is parsed.

features.name: Image pipeline
features.summary: An image pipeline resizes and re-encodes images per device, emits srcset/sizes, and often adds lazy loading and a blur placeholder.
features.whatHtml: An image pipeline resizes and re-encodes images per device, emits srcset/sizes, and often adds lazy loading and a blur placeholder. In principle this item affects LCP more than FCP.
features.gotchasHtml:
• Unpic only builds URLs; something (IPX, a host CDN) still has to serve the resized image.
  • Sharp and IPX do not run on Cloudflare Workers, which is why the Nuxt and SvelteKit ports switch optimization off there.

features.name: Data/HTML caching
features.summary: Caching stores the result of a catalog query or a rendered HTML page so a request does not hit the database again.
features.whatHtml: Caching stores the result of a catalog query or a rendered HTML page so a request does not hit the database again. In principle it shortens time to first byte. A cache that lives in isolate memory does not persist across isolates on a host like Workers, so a portable setup needs persistent KV, Blobs, or Cache-API storage; this repo hand-writes host-specific caches for that reason.
features.gotchasHtml:
• Host cache layers differ (Vercel runtime cache, Netlify Blobs, Cloudflare KV), so a "cache" written for one host needs a storage driver for the others.
  • s-maxage plus stale-while-revalidate only helps if your CDN honors them; TanStack's ISR is a headers pattern, not a framework cache.

features.name: Route prefetching
features.summary: Prefetching loads a route's code and data before the click, on hover, focus, or when the link enters the viewport.
features.whatHtml: Prefetching loads a route's code and data before the click, on hover, focus, or when the link enters the viewport. In principle it helps the next navigation rather than the first paint, so it matters for how fast the app feels once someone starts clicking.
features.gotchasHtml:
• TanStack's preloading is off until you set defaultPreload; Waku's is off until you pass a prop; SvelteKit needs the data-sveltekit-preload-data attribute somewhere (the starter template adds it).
  • Prefetching spends bandwidth on routes the user may never visit; intent (hover/focus) is the conservative setting.

features.name: Islands / partial hydration / lazy slices
features.summary: Normally every interactive component on a page hydrates, so its JavaScript downloads and runs.
features.whatHtml: Normally every interactive component on a page hydrates, so its JavaScript downloads and runs. Islands, deferred hydration, and server islands keep most of the page as plain HTML and hydrate (or render on demand) only the parts that need it. This merged row takes each framework's best label across the partial-hydration and server-island capabilities.
features.gotchasHtml:
• Nuxt nuxt-client hydration and Lazy* hydration only work on SFCs; slot content passed to nuxt-client components is not interactive.
  • <ClientOnly> and clientOnly skip server rendering; they are not deferred hydration.
  • TanStack <Hydrate> and Pracht server islands are newer APIs: check the linked guides for current behavior.

features.name: Per-route render modes
features.summary: A render mode decides when a route's HTML is produced: at build time (static), per request (SSR), on the client (SPA), or revalidated on a schedule.
features.whatHtml: A render mode decides when a route's HTML is produced: at build time (static), per request (SSR), on the client (SPA), or revalidated on a schedule. A per-route switch lets a mostly static site keep one dynamic page without changing the whole app.
features.gotchasHtml:
• With Cache Components on, the dynamic, revalidate, fetchCache, and dynamicParams exports are removed and runtime is unsupported; other segment config such as maxDuration and ensureStatic remains. Do not expect export const dynamic to work.
  • TanStack ssr: false still runs on the client only; 'data-only' is the middle option.
  • Static modes need an adapter that can serve prerendered output on the host you deploy to.

features.name: Art-directed / modern-format images (<picture>)
features.summary: A <picture> element lets the browser choose between formats (AVIF, WebP, JPEG) and, with <source media>, between differently cropped images per breakpoint.
features.whatHtml: A <picture> element lets the browser choose between formats (AVIF, WebP, JPEG) and, with <source media>, between differently cropped images per breakpoint. That second use is "art direction". It matters because bytes and crops both change what the user waits for and sees.
features.gotchasHtml:
• Neither <NuxtPicture> nor enhanced:img does breakpoint art direction; they only negotiate formats and sizes.
  • Hand-written <picture> still needs width/height on the <img> (and on each <source> when the art-directed crops differ in aspect ratio) to avoid layout shift, plus sizes so the browser picks the right srcset candidate.

features.name: Fine-grained client reactivity
features.summary: Fine-grained reactivity tracks dependencies per value, so a state change re-runs only the effects or components that read it; Solid, Svelte, and Marko go furthest and write straight to the affected DOM nodes, while Vue and Angular still update at component granularity (Vue diffs a compiler-optimised virtual DOM) and Qwik falls back to a vDOM for structural changes.
features.whatHtml: Fine-grained reactivity tracks dependencies per value, so a state change re-runs only the effects or components that read it; Solid, Svelte, and Marko go furthest and write straight to the affected DOM nodes, while Vue and Angular still update at component granularity (Vue diffs a compiler-optimised virtual DOM) and Qwik falls back to a vDOM for structural changes. Component-level reactivity (React) re-renders the component and its subtree and diffs the result. This is an interaction-cost property, not a first-paint one: in principle it shows up in INP and memory on long-lived pages.
features.gotchasHtml:
• React Compiler reduces wasted work but components still re-render; the 🧪 reflects that signals for React come only from community packages.
  • This row says nothing about first paint; do not read it as a loading-speed feature.

features.name: Built-in bundle analysis
features.summary: A bundle analyzer shows which modules make up each JavaScript bundle so you can find large dependencies.
features.whatHtml: A bundle analyzer shows which modules make up each JavaScript bundle so you can find large dependencies. Only the Next port has an analysis step configured (pnpm analyze runs next build && next experimental-analyze, the older name for the command the docs now call next analyze); none of the other ports do, so the rest of this section is capability only. Vite DevTools ships DevTools for Rolldown (@vitejs/devtools-rolldown), an ecosystem-level analyzer for production builds on Vite 8+. It is available to the ports on Vite 8 (not the Qwik and Fresh ports, which are on Vite 7) and is not counted in these labels.
features.gotchasHtml:
• Run the analyzer against a production build; development bundles are not representative.
  • Check each tool's own caveats: Astro's recipe, for instance, warns that a visualizer report may not match what the client downloads.

features.name: Third-party script strategies
features.summary: Third-party scripts (analytics, chat widgets, tag managers) compete with your own code.
features.whatHtml: Third-party scripts (analytics, chat widgets, tag managers) compete with your own code. A loading strategy says when each one loads, for example before hydration, after hydration, or at browser idle time. No first-party script primitive is documented for most frameworks here, so ordering and deferral are left to the app.
features.gotchasHtml:
• Next's worker strategy is experimental and pages/-only.
  • Nuxt's partytown option needs @nuxtjs/partytown installed and configured separately.
  • Without a strategy API, ordering and deferral are your job: put async/defer and placement choices in the tag yourself.

features.name: Portable multi-host deployment
features.summary: A host adapter builds your app into the shape a platform expects (Node server, serverless functions, edge Worker).
features.whatHtml: A host adapter builds your app into the shape a platform expects (Node server, serverless functions, edge Worker). A portable framework ships adapters or presets for several hosts, so you can switch without rewriting. That gap is one reason this repo hand-writes host-specific caches.
features.gotchasHtml:
• Presets and adapters change the build output, not your caching: this repo still hand-writes host-specific caches (see section 4).
  • Some host features are experimental or maintained by the host (Next on Cloudflare/Netlify; the Cloudflare and Netlify Vite plugins used by SolidStart and TanStack Start; Waku's Deno, Bun, and Lambda adapters).

cells.label: experimental
cells.bodyHtml:
Set experimental.inlineCss: true in next.config.ts (documented as experimental). One flag.

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  experimental: {
    inlineCss: true,
  },
};

From this repo's next-books/next.config.ts (other options omitted).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
next/font/google self-hosts, subsets, generates the @font-face, and preloads at build time. No config beyond using it in the layout.

import { Geist } from 'next/font/google';

const geistSans = Geist({
  display: 'block',
  subsets: ['latin'],
  variable: '--font-geist-sans',
});

From this repo's next-books/app/layout.tsx (the Geist_Mono import and instance omitted).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Use next/image plus the built-in optimizer, priority on the first ten covers (deprecated in v16 in favour of preload), sizes, and placeholder="blur" fed by ThumbHash data URIs generated by this port's own code.

<Image
  alt={title}
  blurDataURL={thumbhash ? createPngDataUri(thumbhash) : undefined}
  fill
  placeholder={thumbhash ? 'blur' : 'empty'}
  priority={priority}
  sizes={sizes}
  src={resolved}
/>

From this repo's next-books/features/book/components/book-cover.tsx (some props omitted).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Turn on cacheComponents: true (enabled here), then mark queries with 'use cache' and cacheLife('hours').

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
};
export async function getBooksPage(query: BookQuery): Promise<BookSummary[]> {
  'use cache';
  cacheLife('hours');
  // ...query the database
}

From this repo's next-books/next.config.ts (other options omitted) and features/book/book-queries.ts (query body omitted).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Set partialPrefetching (needs cacheComponents; 16.3+), pass prefetch={true} on high-value links (<Link>), and optionally add the FastLink mouse-down navigation.

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
};
<FastLink href={href} prefetch={true}>

Adapted from this repo's next-books/next.config.ts (other options omitted) and features/book/components/book-pagination.tsx (href expression simplified; other props omitted); FastLink is this repo's wrapper around Link.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Server Components keep a component's JavaScript out of the browser (server and client components). Every Client Component still hydrates: no hydrate-on-visible/idle/never control is documented (next/dynamic with ssr: false is client-only rendering, not deferred hydration), although React hydrates each <Suspense> boundary as its own unit and prioritizes the one being interacted with (streaming guide). Enabling cacheComponents: true (the same flag as in section 4, enabled here) renders a cached shell and fills request-time holes. That is functionally close to a server island, but the API is an uncached data boundary inside Suspense, not a named island with its own cache entry.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Next documents stable per-route exports: without Cache Components, dynamic and revalidate (previous-model guide); with Cache Components, ensureStatic (v16.4.0+, not in this port's pinned canary) plus 'use cache' boundaries (see section 4). This port enables Cache Components, where dynamic, revalidate, fetchCache, and dynamicParams are removed (route segment config). No inline example (unsourced).

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml:
getImageProps() returns per-breakpoint props; you hand-write the <picture> and <source> elements (hence 🔧). getImageProps() is stable (v14.1.0) and the built-in optimizer already negotiates AVIF/WebP from the Accept header; this row scores only whether the framework emits a <picture> for you.

const {
  props: { srcSet: desktop },
} = getImageProps({ ...common, width: 1440, height: 875, quality: 80, src: '/desktop.jpg' })
const {
  props: { srcSet: mobile, ...rest },
} = getImageProps({ ...common, width: 750, height: 1334, quality: 70, src: '/mobile.jpg' })

return (
  <picture>
    <source media="(min-width: 1000px)" srcSet={desktop} />
    <source media="(min-width: 500px)" srcSet={mobile} />
    <img {...rest} style={{ width: '100%', height: 'auto' }} />
  </picture>
)

Adapted from the image docs, where common is { alt: 'Art Direction Example', sizes: '100vw' }.

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml:
React re-renders component subtrees; fine-grained updates need a community signals package such as @preact/signals-react (hence 🧪; not used in this port). reactCompiler: true (stable since v16.0.0) is enabled in this repo and auto-memoizes, but it does not change the re-render model.

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  reactCompiler: true,
};

From this repo's next-books/next.config.ts (other options omitted).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
The Turbopack bundle analyzer (guide) shipped in v16.1 as next experimental-analyze and is next analyze as of v16.4.0 (the old name remains an alias). It opens the Turbopack module graph with per-route client/server filtering; --output saves a static report and next analyze export (v16.4.0+) streams the saved data. This port is pinned to 16.4.0-canary.8, where the command is still next experimental-analyze and export is not available. The same guide covers the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin for webpack builds.

npx next analyze
npx next analyze --output

From the package bundling guide.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Use next/script with beforeInteractive, afterInteractive, and lazyOnload strategies for the App Router. worker is experimental, pages/-only, and needs experimental.nextScriptWorkers. The experimental @next/third-parties (guide) wraps common embeds.

import Script from 'next/script'

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <>
      <Script src="https://example.com/script.js" strategy="lazyOnload" />
    </>
  )
}

From the Script docs.

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml:
A stable Adapter API (adapterPath, v16.2+) with verified Vercel and Bun adapters; Cloudflare and Netlify "are working on verified adapters" (deploying). They use their own integrations today: OpenNext for Cloudflare and @netlify/plugin-nextjs for Netlify in this port. output: 'standalone' covers self-hosting, though this port does not set it.

const nextConfig = {
  adapterPath: require.resolve('./my-adapter.js'),
}

Adapted from the adapterPath docs.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Set features.inlineStyles: true, but only on this repo's nuxt-books-optimized-max branch; the plain optimized build leaves the global stylesheet linked.

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  features: {
    // Production SSR embeds entry and component CSS in the HTML.
    inlineStyles: true,
  },
});

From this repo's nuxt-books/nuxt.config.ts (nuxt-books-optimized-max branch).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Add the official @nuxt/fonts module. It resolves the fonts used in CSS, downloads them at build time, serves them from your own origin, injects @font-face rules, generates fallback metrics for lower CLS, and can subset.

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: [
    '@nuxt/fonts',
  ]
})

Adapted from the module page. This port does not use it; it imports @fontsource-variable/geist manually, so the capability exists in the framework even though this repo took the third-party route:

@import '@fontsource-variable/geist';

From this repo's nuxt-books/app/assets/css/main.css (optimized branch).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Install @nuxt/image (separate official module) and use <NuxtImg preload> on the first covers.

modules: ['@nuxt/image'],
image: {
  provider: isCloudflare ? 'none' : 'auto',
  quality: 82,
},
<NuxtImg :src="source" :sizes="sizes" :preload="priority" :width="400" :height="600" />

From this repo's nuxt-books/nuxt.config.ts (nuxt-books-optimized-max branch) and app/components/BookCover.vue (optimized branch; some props and options omitted).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Wrap handlers in defineCachedEventHandler (the Nitro v2 API that this Nuxt 4 port runs on, nitropack 2.13.4; Nitro v3 calls it defineCachedHandler), configure nitro.storage.cache, and add a header-only routeRules cache. The optimized branch uses the Vercel runtime cache, and the max branch adds Netlify Blobs and Cloudflare KV drivers.

export default defineCachedEventHandler(
  async event => { /* ... */ },
  {
    getKey: event => hashCacheKey(/* filters from the query */),
    maxAge: 60 * 60,
    name: 'books-count',
    swr: true,
  },
);
routeRules: {
  '/**': { cache: { headersOnly: true, maxAge: 3600 } },
  '/api/**': { cache: false },
},

From this repo's nuxt-books/server/api/books/count.get.ts (optimized branch; handler body elided) and nuxt.config.ts (nuxt-books-optimized-max branch).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Use <NuxtLink> prefetch-on="visibility" | "interaction", _payload.json payload prefetch, and experimental.prefetchPreloadTags (experimental, off by default).

<FastLink :prefetch-on="eagerPrefetch ? 'visibility' : 'interaction'" :to="href">
experimental: {
  prefetchPreloadTags: true,
},

From this repo's nuxt-books/app/components/BookCard.vue (FastLink is this repo's wrapper around NuxtLink; class omitted) and nuxt.config.ts (optimized branch; early404 omitted).

cells.label: experimental
cells.bodyHtml:
Documented lazy hydration (hydrate-on-visible, -on-idle, -on-interaction, -on-media-query, hydrate-never on Lazy* components, SFC only; on by default; the switch is experimental.lazyHydration) and features.noScripts / noScripts:

<template>
  <div>
    <LazyMyComponent hydrate-on-visible />
  </div>
</template>

Adapted from the components docs. Server components and islands stay experimental: server components and islands render a component with no client JS; prop changes refetch the island (<NuxtIsland>), and props travel as query parameters so island responses can be cached by a CDN. nuxt-client selective hydration works only on local .vue SFCs, and slots passed to nuxt-client components are server-rendered and not interactive.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
routeRules: globs map to prerender, swr, isr, ssr: false, cache headers, redirects, and proxy rules.

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  routeRules: {
    '/admin/**': { ssr: false },
  },
})

Adapted from the rendering docs. This port uses a header-only cache rule on /** (needed for _payload.json prefetch) and disables caching on /api/**, shown in section 4.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
<NuxtPicture> serves modern formats with a fallback via @nuxt/image; its docs say it does not support multiple image sources, so no breakpoint art direction.

<NuxtPicture
  format="avif,webp"
  src="/nuxt-icon.png"
/>

From the NuxtPicture docs.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Vue's ref/reactive tracks dependencies and updates the affected effects. Nothing to enable.

const value = ref('');

From this repo's nuxt-books/app/components/BookSearch.vue (optimized branch).

cells.label: experimental
cells.bodyHtml:
nuxt analyze (experimental) builds the app and serves client and Nitro reports; --json writes machine-readable output.

npx nuxt analyze [ROOTDIR] [--serve] [--prerender] [--json]

Adapted from the analyze command docs (other flags omitted). With Nuxt 5 behaviour the Nitro report needs rollup-plugin-visualizer. The non-experimental build.analyze config option also writes a client-bundle report during a normal nuxt build; with the default Vite builder it loads the community rollup-plugin-visualizer, which must be installed in the project (optional peer dependency), so the cell stays 🧪.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
@nuxt/scripts is a separate official module (modules page, GitHub) with per-script strategy and proxying; useScript's partytown option loads a script in a web worker and needs @nuxtjs/partytown installed and configured separately.

const { onLoaded, onError, status } = useScript('https://example.com/sdk.js')

From the useScript docs.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Nitro presets cover every host this repo targets (Node, Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare). Vercel and Netlify auto-detect their presets; force Workers explicitly:

nitro: {
  preset: isCloudflare ? 'cloudflare_module' : undefined,
},

From this repo's nuxt-books/nuxt.config.ts (nuxt-books-optimized-max branch).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Set inlineStyleThreshold high enough (e.g. Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY; the docs define it as the max CSS file length in UTF-16 code units) in vite.config.ts. One line, but you have to know it exists.

sveltekit({
  inlineStyleThreshold: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
})

From this repo's svelte-books/vite.config.ts (optimized branch).

cells.label: third-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Import @fontsource-variable/geist (Fontsource). SvelteKit has no first-party font module and does not preload fonts by default; the handle hook's resolve(..., { preload }) filter can add font preloads (not used here), so the font is discovered from the inlined stylesheet.

@import "@fontsource-variable/geist";

From this repo's svelte-books/src/routes/layout.css (optimized branch).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
The framework offers @sveltejs/enhanced-img, a build-time plugin that only optimizes image files present at build. For remote images such as this port's covers the same page points to a CDN and names the community @unpic/svelte, so this port uses Unpic transforms plus an ipx handler (src/lib/server/ipx-handler.ts), disabled on Cloudflare. adapter-vercel also has an images option (not used here). To use the first-party route for local files:

enhancedImages(), // must come before the SvelteKit plugin
<enhanced:img src="./path/to/your/image.jpg" alt="An alt text" />

Adapted from the images docs.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Use adapter-vercel's per-route isr option, exported as config from a route, as done in src/lib/server/page-isr.ts. SvelteKit also has first-party, host-independent pieces: setHeaders in load for cache-control (this port sets it in src/routes/+layout.server.ts) and per-route prerender. The experimental remote functions only dedupe a query within one request (and share it on the client while it is in use); their prerender variant stores build-time data. This port turns on the remoteFunctions flag but defines no remote functions. A cross-request data cache on other hosts is manual: src/lib/server/catalog-cache.ts with Vercel Cache, Netlify Blobs, and the Workers KV/Cache API paths.

export const catalogIsrConfig = {
  isr: { expiration: CATALOG_CACHE_REVALIDATE_SECONDS, allowQuery: ['page', 'search'] }
} satisfies Config;
// src/routes/+page.server.ts
export const config = catalogIsrConfig;

From this repo's svelte-books/src/lib/server/page-isr.ts and src/routes/+page.server.ts (optimized branch; allowQuery shortened and spread removed).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Set data-sveltekit-preload-data="hover". This repo's FastLink wrapper maps a preload prop to that attribute per link ('hover' or 'off'); the pagination and sidebar links pass it explicitly and book cards pass preload={eagerPrefetch}. The starter template already sets the attribute on <body>, and JS/CSS are preloaded automatically (performance).

<body data-sveltekit-preload-data="hover">

From this repo's svelte-books/src/app.html (optimized branch; class attribute omitted).

export const csr = false;

export const prerender = true;
export const ssr = false;
export const csr = false;

From the page options docs (each is a separate option; combine as needed).

Pick an adapter for Node, Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare, or static output.

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml:
There is no first-party production inlining flag documented in the styling and assets docs (Solid 2 start mode, this port's stack; production output is <link rel="stylesheet"> tags) or in the archived SolidStart v2 CSS and styling docs, so you wire it yourself: import the stylesheet with ?inline (a Vite CSS feature) and render it in a <style> tag.

import appCss from "./app.css?inline";
// ...
<NoHydration>
  <style>{import.meta.env.SSR ? appCss : ""}</style>
</NoHydration>

From this repo's solid-books/src/Document.tsx (optimized branch). NoHydration keeps the CSS string out of the client bundle.

import geistLatin from "@fontsource-variable/geist/files/geist-latin-wght-normal.woff2?url";
// ...
<link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" href={geistLatin} crossorigin="" />

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
The Solid team publishes @solidjs/image (npm latest 1.0.0 for Solid 2; 0.x for Solid 1): a SolidImage component plus imagePlugin from @solidjs/image/vite, which resizes and re-encodes local images at build time with sharp, emits srcset, lazy-loads, and supports blur/BlurHash/ThumbHash previews. It is not mentioned on docs.solidjs.com (package README only). This port does not use it, or Unpic; it uses a custom imageSrcset helper plus the per-host Nitro image config and cover preload components. The Vercel half of that Nitro config looks like this:

nitro({
  vercel: {
    config: {
      version: 3,
      images: {
        sizes: IMAGE_WIDTHS,
        formats: ["image/avif", "image/webp"],
      },
    },
  },
}),

From this repo's solid-books/vite.config.ts (optimized branch; domains, remotePatterns, minimumCacheTTL and the Netlify block omitted).

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml:
Nitro routeRules (swr, cache) and defineCachedHandler are available, but this port configures none, so loaders in src/features/book/book-queries.ts query Postgres on a cold request. Solid Router's first-party query cache dedupes and caches client-side data. Route pre-rendering covers any route listed in routes or crawled via nitro.prerender.

routeRules: {
  "/blog/**": { swr: 3600 },
},

Adapted from the Nitro cache docs; this port does not set it.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Solid Router v1 and the 2.0.0-next.21 prerelease this port pins preload on hover (~20ms) and focus by default. In Solid Router 2.0 stable (npm latest 2.0.1) link preloading is opt-in: createRouter({ routes, preloadLinks: intentPreload() }), with tapPreload, viewportPreload and eagerPreload as other strategies. usePreloadRoute is the manual API, and this port's FastLink calls it on hover and focus (and eagerly when its prefetch prop is set), and starts the navigation on mouse-down.

import { useNavigate, usePreloadRoute } from "@solidjs/router";

From this repo's solid-books/src/components/ui/fast-link.tsx (optimized branch).

cells.label: experimental
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party islands are documented: released SolidStart v2 reserves experimental.islands and only accepts false (config reference). Solid 2's @solidjs/web has experimental server components (a component returned from a "use server" function and mounted with dynamicComponent; docs), not used by this port. clientOnly skips SSR for a single component, which is not islands. No inline example (unsourced).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Route prerendering is set under top-level nitro: { prerender: { routes, crawlLinks } } in v2/vite-plugin setups, and Nitro routeRules can set swr/cache per route (see the snippet in section 4); there is no per-route SSR/SPA switch. For the Solid 2 stack, see deployment (top-level nitro config) and choose a rendering mode (prerender-crawler).

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [solidStart(), nitro()],
  nitro: {
    prerender: {
      routes: ["/", "/about"],
    },
  },
});

From the archived SolidStart v2 route pre-rendering docs (uses @solidjs/start, not this port's @solidjs/vite-plugin setup).

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: SolidImage from the Solid team's @solidjs/image renders a <picture> with one <source> per output format (default webp + jpeg, AVIF available) and a merged srcset; that is modern formats and sizes, not breakpoint art direction. The package is documented in its README only, not on docs.solidjs.com. This port does not use it and builds srcset with its own imageSrcset helper. No inline example (unsourced).

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party script-loading strategy is documented (head and metadata); Script from @solidjs/meta only emits a <script> tag (reference). Nothing to enable.
cells.exampleHtml:
Write the tags in the port's Document.tsx, next to its inline theme script. For a lazy strategy, add an inline loader that injects the third-party script once the page is idle.

// src/Document.tsx
const themeScript = `(function(){ /* … from the port … */ })();`;
const lazyAnalytics = `addEventListener("load",function(){(window.requestIdleCallback||setTimeout)(function(){var s=document.createElement("script");s.src="https://example-analytics.com/script.js";s.async=true;document.head.appendChild(s);});});`;

export default function Document(props: ParentProps) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        {/* … meta, font preload, inlined CSS from the port … */}
        <script>{themeScript}</script>
        <script src="https://example.com/critical.js" async />
        <script>{lazyAnalytics}</script>
        <HydrationScript />
      </head>
      <body>{props.children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}

None of them is maintained by the Solid team, so the cell is scored 🧪, as for React Router's host-maintained integrations.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Use static prerendering plus per-route Cache-Control / stale-while-revalidate headers, which the ISR guide describes; the CDN does the revalidating, so there is no framework data cache.

export const Route = createFileRoute('/posts/$id')({
  headers: () => ({
    'Cache-Control': 'public, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400',
  }),
})

From the ISR guide (its Vercel example; the guide's generic example also sets max-age=3600). This port uses src/lib/catalog-cache.ts plus a request middleware that sets document Cache-Control headers in src/start.ts:

const result = await next()
const headers = new Headers(result.response.headers)
headers.set('Cache-Control', hostDocumentCacheControl())

From this repo's tanstack-books/src/start.ts (optimized branch; abridged).

const router = createTanStackRouter({
  routeTree,

cells.label: experimental
cells.bodyHtml:
<Hydrate when={visible()}> keeps the server HTML, splits the child into its own chunk, and defers hydration (load, idle, visible, media, interaction, condition, never).

import { Hydrate } from '@tanstack/react-start'
import { visible } from '@tanstack/react-start/hydration'

<Hydrate when={visible()}>
  <Reviews />
</Hydrate>

From the deferred hydration guide. <ClientOnly> is different: it skips SSR rather than deferring hydration. Experimental Server Components are also available via rsc: { enabled: true } and @vitejs/plugin-rsc. This port uses neither.

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml:
Per-route ssr: true | false | 'data-only' with a defaultSsr, plus a global SPA mode. Prerendering is configured in the plugin, and ISR is a headers pattern rather than a render mode.

export const startInstance = createStart(() => ({
  defaultSsr: false,
}))
export const Route = createFileRoute('/posts/$postId')({
  ssr: false,
  component: () => <div>This component is rendered on the client</div>,
})

From the selective SSR guide. The guide says 'data-only' keeps beforeLoad and loader on the server while skipping server rendering of the component.

cells.bodyHtml: Nothing to enable: no first-party <picture> component is documented (production checklist). Third-party @unpic/react exports a <Source> component (media, type) for use inside a hand-written <picture>; this port does not use it, and because the <picture> is still hand-written the cell stays 🔧, as for Next's getImageProps().
cells.exampleHtml:
Wrap the port's Unpic <Image> in a hand-written <picture>, and add <Source> from @unpic/react for each art-directed variant. Pass <Source> the same CDN settings the port's Image wrapper uses.

// src/features/book/components/book-cover.tsx
import { Source } from '@unpic/react'
import { Image } from '@/components/ui/image'
import { imageCdn } from '@/lib/image-config'
// …
const small = src ?? EMPTY_IMAGE_URL
const size = { layout: 'constrained', width: COVER_IMAGE_WIDTH, height: COVER_IMAGE_HEIGHT } as const

return (
  <picture>
    <Source
      {...size}
      media="(min-width: 768px)"
      src={getLargeBookImageUrl(small)}
      cdn={imageCdn}
      options={imageCdn === 'ipx' ? { ipx: { baseURL: '/_ipx' } } : undefined}
    />
    <Image {...size} alt={title} src={small} sizes={sizes} priority={priority}
           className="absolute inset-0 size-full object-cover" objectFit="cover" unstyled />
  </picture>
)

cells.bodyHtml: React. The React Compiler is not enabled in this port (vite.config.ts calls viteReact() with no compiler option and adds no reactCompilerPreset Babel plugin), so state updates re-render component subtrees. The compiler is opt-in and would not change the model. Fine-grained updates need a community signals library such as @preact/signals-react (hence 🧪 third-party); nothing first-party provides them. No inline example (unsourced for this port).

  const { cloudflare } = await import('@cloudflare/vite-plugin')
  plugins.push(cloudflare({ viteEnvironment: { name: 'ssr' } }))
} else if (isNetlify) {

  plugins.push(netlify())
} else {

}

cells.exampleHtml:
React 19 hoists an <script async src> rendered anywhere into <head> and deduplicates it. For a lazy strategy, write a small client component that injects the tag after load.

// src/components/lazy-script.tsx
'use client';
import { useEffect } from 'react';

export function LazyScript({ src }: { src: string }) {
  useEffect(() => {
    const inject = () => {
      if (document.querySelector(`script[src="${src}"]`)) return;
      const s = Object.assign(document.createElement('script'), { src, async: true });
      document.head.append(s);
    };
    const idle = () => ('requestIdleCallback' in window ? requestIdleCallback(inject) : setTimeout(inject));
    if (document.readyState === 'complete') idle();
    else addEventListener('load', idle, { once: true });
  }, [src]);
  return null;
}

// src/pages/_layout.tsx
<script async src="https://example.com/critical.js" />        {/* afterInteractive-ish */}
<LazyScript src="https://example-analytics.com/script.js" />  {/* lazyOnload */}

cells.exampleHtml:
The port's build step already rewrites the HTML template. Extend it to swap the built stylesheet <link> for a <style> tag. The Node, Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare deploys all use that template, so they all get the inlined CSS.

// scripts/prepare-server-template.mjs
import { mkdir, readFile, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';

const root = process.cwd();
const clientIndex = resolve(root, 'dist/client/index.html');
const serverTemplate = resolve(root, 'dist/server/template.html');

let html = await readFile(clientIndex, 'utf8');
const link = html.match(/<link[^>]+href="(\/assets\/[^"]+\.css)"[^>]*>/);
if (link) {
  const css = await readFile(resolve(root, 'dist/client', link[1].slice(1)), 'utf8');
  html = html.replace(link[0], `<style>${css}</style>`);
}

await mkdir(resolve(root, 'dist/server'), { recursive: true });
await writeFile(serverTemplate, html);
await rm(clientIndex);

cells.exampleHtml:
Write an ember-modifier that starts the book request on hover or focus and caches the promise. The route's model hook then reads the same cached promise. <LinkTo> passes the modifier through to its <a>.

// app/lib/book/load-catalog.js
const bookCache = new Map();
export function prefetchBook(id, searchParams) {
  const key = `${id}?${stringifySearchParams(searchParams)}`;
  if (!bookCache.has(key)) bookCache.set(key, loadBook(id, searchParams));
  return bookCache.get(key);
}

// app/modifiers/prefetch-book.js
import { modifier } from 'ember-modifier';
import { prefetchBook } from '../lib/book/load-catalog';

export default modifier((element, [id, searchParams]) => {
  const warm = () => prefetchBook(id, searchParams);
  element.addEventListener('pointerenter', warm, { once: true });
  element.addEventListener('focus', warm, { once: true });
  return () => {
    element.removeEventListener('pointerenter', warm);
    element.removeEventListener('focus', warm);
  };
});

// app/routes/book.js: model(params) { return prefetchBook(params.id, parseSearchParams(params)); }
// app/components/book/book-card.gjs
<LinkTo @route="book" @model={{this.bookId}} @query={{this.query}}
        {{prefetchBook this.bookId @searchParams}}>
  {{! … }}
</LinkTo>

cells.exampleHtml:
Serve the page with a small entry instead of app/entry.js. Then mount each interactive component into its placeholder with renderComponent from @ember/renderer. The rest of the page stays static HTML.

// app/islands.js (the only <script type="module"> on a static page)
import { renderComponent } from '@ember/renderer';
import FavoriteButton from './components/islands/favorite-button';

const islands = { 'favorite-button': FavoriteButton };

for (const el of document.querySelectorAll('[data-island]')) {
  const args = JSON.parse(el.dataset.args ?? '{}');
  el.replaceChildren(); // no hydration: drop the server markup, then render fresh
  renderComponent(islands[el.dataset.island], { into: el, args });
}

// app/components/islands/favorite-button.gjs
import Component from '@glimmer/component';
import { tracked } from '@glimmer/tracking';
import { on } from '@ember/modifier';

export default class FavoriteButton extends Component {
  @tracked saved = false;
  toggle = () => (this.saved = !this.saved);
  <template>
    <button type="button" {{on "click" this.toggle}}>
      {{if this.saved "Saved" "Save"}} {{@title}}
    </button>
  </template>
}

Source: RFC 1099: renderComponent

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: SSR is app-wide in this port (emberSsr() from community vite-ember-ssr; official FastBoot is also app-wide). vite-ember-ssr can additionally prerender a listed set of routes at build time (emberSsg({ routes })), a community build step (React Router's equivalent first-party prerender list is what earns its ✅); no first-party per-route render mode is documented, so nothing to enable.
cells.exampleHtml:
Choose the mode per path in the port's request handler. Server-render the routes that need it. For the rest, return the unrendered template: the same SPA shell the port's Netlify and Cloudflare deploys serve.

// server/handle-request.js
const CLIENT_ONLY = [/^\/account(\/|$)/]; // example: routes that skip SSR

export async function handleFetch(request, options = {}) {
  const url = new URL(request.url);
  // … /api/* handlers from the port …

  const template = await getTemplate();
  if (CLIENT_ONLY.some((re) => re.test(url.pathname))) {
    // SPA shell: app/entry.js boots the app in the browser
    return new Response(template, {
      headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8' },
    });
  }

  const emberApp = await getEmberApp();
  const rendered = await emberApp.renderRoute(`${url.pathname}${url.search}`, {
    settledTimeout: 8000,
  });
  return new Response(assembleHTML(template, rendered), {
    headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8' },
    status: rendered.statusCode,
  });
}

cells.bodyHtml: Embroider/Vite (guide) plus a community SSR layer (vite-ember-ssr here; in this port only the Node server and the Vercel function server-render, while the Netlify and Cloudflare deploys serve a static SPA shell plus API functions). Official FastBoot 6.0.0 documents Ember CLI builds only; Vite-app support is an open draft PR. No first-party host adapters are documented (FastBoot's deploy page covers a Node app server plus Heroku- and community-maintained AWS integrations, not Vercel, Netlify, or Cloudflare), so nothing to enable.
cells.exampleHtml:
From the port: each host gets its own entry file and config, written by hand. Vercel runs the SSR handler as a function (vercel.json rewrites everything to /api). Cloudflare runs a Worker that serves the API and the static SPA shell. Netlify uses netlify.toml redirects plus netlify/functions/api.mjs.

// api/index.js (Vercel: SSR + API)
import '../server/load-env.js';
import { handleNodeRequest } from '../server/handle-request.js';
export default handleNodeRequest;

// workers/index.mjs (Cloudflare: API only, assets from dist/client)
import { bookPayload, catalogPayload, searchParamsFromUrl } from '../server/catalog-api.js';

export default {
  async fetch(request, env) {
    if (env?.POSTGRES_URL) process.env.POSTGRES_URL = env.POSTGRES_URL;
    const url = new URL(request.url);
    if (url.pathname === '/api/catalog') {
      return Response.json(await catalogPayload(searchParamsFromUrl(url.href)));
    }
    // … /api/books/:id …
    return env.ASSETS.fetch(request); // SPA shell (not_found_handling: single-page-application)
  },
};

cells.exampleHtml:
There is no image component, so write <picture> in a route or component, with files served from public/. React spells the attribute srcSet.

// app/features/home/hero-image.tsx
export function HeroImage() {
  return (
    <picture>
      {/* art direction: a square crop on narrow screens */}
      <source media="(max-width: 640px)" type="image/avif"
              srcSet="/media/hero-square-640.avif" width={640} height={640} />
      {/* format fallback: AVIF, then WebP, then the <img> JPEG */}
      <source type="image/avif" sizes="100vw"
              srcSet="/media/hero-1280.avif 1280w, /media/hero-1920.avif 1920w" />
      <source type="image/webp" sizes="100vw"
              srcSet="/media/hero-1280.webp 1280w, /media/hero-1920.webp 1920w" />
      <img src="/media/hero-1280.jpg" alt="Shelves of books" width={1280} height={720}
           fetchPriority="high" decoding="async" />
    </picture>
  )
}

// app/root.tsx
import { useEffect } from 'react'
// …
export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        {/* … */}
        {/* React 19 hoists and de-duplicates <script async src> */}
        <script async src="https://plausible.io/js/script.js" data-domain="books.example" />
      </head>
      {/* … */}
    </html>
  )
}

export default function App() {
  useEffect(() => {
    // Client only, after hydration: load the chat widget when the browser is idle.
    ;(window.requestIdleCallback ?? setTimeout)(() => {
      const s = document.createElement('script')
      s.src = 'https://widget.example.com/chat.js'
      s.async = true
      document.body.append(s)
    })
  }, [])
  // …
}

  selector: 'app-hero-image',

cells.bodyHtml: No first-party script-loading primitive documented (the runtime-performance page lists none). Rests on absence. (runtime-performance)
cells.exampleHtml:
Put the loading strategy in the tag yourself: async in src/index.html for early scripts, or afterNextRender to inject one after the first browser render.

// src/index.html: loads in parallel, runs as soon as it arrives
// <script async src="https://plausible.io/js/script.js" data-domain="books.example"></script>

// src/app/app.ts: load a chat widget only in the browser, after first render
import { Component, afterNextRender } from '@angular/core';

@Component({ selector: 'app-root', templateUrl: './app.html' })
export class App {
  constructor() {
    afterNextRender(() => {
      // Never runs during SSR; wait for idle so the widget doesn't compete with hydration.
      (window.requestIdleCallback ?? setTimeout)(() => {
        const s = document.createElement('script');
        s.src = 'https://widget.example.com/chat.js';
        s.async = true;
        document.body.append(s);
      });
    });
  }
}

Vercel lists Angular only as a zero-config frontend framework and no Vercel Angular SSR page was found, so the four hosts this repo targets are not all covered. The deployment page also lists third-party ng deploy builders. This portability judgment is lower confidence. (ssr, angular, angular, frontend, deployment)

From the port: one AngularAppEngine handler per host, each picked by a build configuration in angular.json. Vercel reuses the Node/Express build behind a function.

// angular-books/src/server.cloudflare.ts (Netlify's server.netlify.ts is the same shape)
import { AngularAppEngine, createRequestHandler } from '@angular/ssr';
// …
const angularAppEngine = new AngularAppEngine();

async function handle(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const result = await angularAppEngine.handle(request);
  return result || new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });
}

export const reqHandler = createRequestHandler(handle);
export default { fetch: (request: Request) => handle(request) };

// angular-books/angular.json, build.configurations: one SSR entry per host
// "node":       { "ssr": { "entry": "src/server.ts" } },
// "cloudflare": { "ssr": { "entry": "src/server.cloudflare.ts", "platform": "neutral" } },
// "netlify":    {}  // default "ssr.entry": "src/server.netlify.ts"

Marko Run navigates with full documents, so a Speculation Rules block in the layout handles it. Supporting browsers prefetch same-origin links on hover; the others ignore the block.

// src/routes/+layout.marko
<head>
  // …
  <html-script type="speculationrules">
    {
      "prefetch": [{
        "where": { "and": [
          { "href_matches": "/*" },
          { "not": { "selector_matches": "[rel~=nofollow]" } }
        ]},
        "eagerness": "moderate"
      }]
    }
  </html-script>
</head>

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: Marko Run documents streaming SSR; the static adapter is app-wide and +meta.* is static metadata only. No per-route render-mode switch documented. (file-based-routing, adapters)
cells.exampleHtml:
Every route still streams SSR. You tag a route with a mode in +meta.json, and the root middleware turns it into CDN Cache-Control. This adapts the port's +middleware.ts.

// src/routes/about/+meta.json   →  { "render": "static" }
// src/routes/+meta.json         →  { "render": "isr" }

// src/routes/+middleware.ts
const cacheControl: Record<string, string> = {
  static: "public, s-maxage=31536000",                // cached until redeploy
  isr: "public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=86400",
};

export default Run.ALL(async (ctx, next) => {
  const res = await next();
  if (!res.headers.get("content-type")?.includes("text/html")) return res;
  const mode = (ctx.meta as { render?: string } | undefined)?.render;
  const headers = new Headers(res.headers);
  headers.set("Cache-Control", cacheControl[mode ?? ""] ?? "private, no-store"); // SSR
  return new Response(res.body, { status: res.status, statusText: res.statusText, headers });
});

  alt: string;
  priority?: boolean;
}

<picture>
  <source media="(min-width: 1000px)" type="image/avif" srcset="/hero-wide.avif">
  <source media="(min-width: 1000px)" srcset="/hero-wide.jpg">
  <source type="image/avif" srcset="/hero-tall.avif">
  <img
    src="/hero-tall.jpg"
    alt=input.alt
    width=750
    height=1334
    decoding="async"
    fetchpriority=(input.priority ? "high" : undefined)
    loading=(input.priority ? "eager" : "lazy")

cells.exampleHtml:
You wrap each query in a TTL cache backed by a host store, and set the HTML Cache-Control in app middleware. This comes from the port.

// lib/catalog-cache.server.ts
export function withTtlCache<Args extends unknown[], Result>(
  name: string,
  fn: (...args: Args) => Promise<Result>,
): (...args: Args) => Promise<Result> {
  // in-memory Map → Workers KV / Vercel getCache / Netlify Blobs → fn()
  return (...args: Args) => cacheLifeHours(`${name}:${JSON.stringify(args)}`, () => fn(...args))
}

// features/book/book-queries.server.ts
export const getBooksPage = withTtlCache('getBooksPage', getBooksPageUncached)

// main.ts
app.use(async (ctx) => {
  const res = await ctx.next();
  if (!res.headers.get("content-type")?.includes("text/html")) return res;
  const headers = new Headers(res.headers);
  headers.set("Cache-Control", hostDocumentCacheControl());
  return new Response(res.body, { status: res.status, statusText: res.statusText, headers });
});

cells.label: first-party
cells.bodyHtml: Islands are the core model: only island JS ships and bundles are code-split; files live in islands/ or (_islands); props must be serializable. No lazy/idle/visible hydration timing is documented; Preact lazy() + <Suspense> is documented for code-splitting an island. (islands, architecture, common-patterns)

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: Pages render to HTML on the server; no per-route prerender/SPA/ISR option is documented (RouteConfig covers routeOverride, skipAppWrapper, skipInheritedLayouts, csp and methods; none selects a render mode). No first-party per-route render mode documented. (architecture, routing, file-routing)
cells.exampleHtml:
Every route still renders on the server. You pick a mode per route with CDN Cache-Control headers in app middleware, adapting the port's main.ts middleware.

// main.ts
const modes: Record<string, string> = {
  "/about": "public, s-maxage=31536000",                    // "static": cached until redeploy
  "/": "public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=86400", // "ISR": revalidate each minute
};

app.use(async (ctx) => {
  const res = await ctx.next();
  if (!res.headers.get("content-type")?.includes("text/html")) return res;
  const headers = new Headers(res.headers);
  headers.set("Cache-Control", modes[ctx.url.pathname] ?? "private, no-store"); // SSR
  return new Response(res.body, { status: res.status, statusText: res.statusText, headers });
});

app.fsRoutes();

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party <picture> component documented; the docs point to vite-imagetools or a CDN, with markup hand-written. (static-files)
cells.exampleHtml:
You write the <picture> markup in a Preact component and put each pre-encoded format and crop in static/ yourself.

// components/Hero.tsx
export function Hero() {
  return (
    <picture>
      <source media="(min-width: 1000px)" type="image/avif" srcset="/hero-wide.avif" />
      <source media="(min-width: 1000px)" srcset="/hero-wide.jpg" />
      <source type="image/avif" srcset="/hero-tall.avif" />
      <img
        src="/hero-tall.jpg"
        alt="Shelves of books"
        width={750}
        height={1334}
        fetchPriority="high"
        decoding="async"
      />
    </picture>
  );
}

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: No first-party script primitive documented; the head page lists <script> with no loading-strategy guidance. (head)
cells.exampleHtml:
You write the loading strategy into <head> in _app.tsx. Use async or defer on the tag, or inject it at idle time with an inline script, as the port does for its theme script.

// routes/_app.tsx
const loadChatWhenIdle = `(window.requestIdleCallback||setTimeout)(function(){
  var s=document.createElement("script");s.src="https://widget.example.com/chat.js";s.async=true;
  document.head.appendChild(s);});`;

export default define.page(function App({ Component }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        {/* … */}
        <script async src="https://analytics.example.com/script.js" />      {/* parallel, non-blocking */}
        <script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: loadChatWhenIdle }} />   {/* after load, at idle */}
      </head>
      {/* <head> sits outside <Partial>, so f-client-nav does not re-run these */}
      <body f-client-nav>{/* … */}</body>
    </html>
  );
});

cells.label: manual
cells.bodyHtml: Documented: Deno Deploy, deno compile, Docker, and Cloudflare Workers (via @cloudflare/vite-plugin and a hand-written server.js; stability not stated). Node, Vercel, and Netlify are not documented; no official guide was found. (deployment, cloudflare-workers, docker, deno-deploy)
cells.exampleHtml:
You write a post-build script that wraps _fresh/server.js in each host's entry shape. This comes from the port: an edge function for Netlify, and a Node handler plus Build Output API config for Vercel.

// scripts/netlify-edge.mjs
import server from "../_fresh/server.js";
export default (request) => server.fetch(request);

// scripts/adapt.mjs (runs after `vite build`; host picked by NETLIFY=1 | VERCEL=1)
if (host === "vercel") {
  await build({ ...common, entryPoints: ["scripts/vercel-handler.mjs"],
    outfile: `${out}/functions/index.func/index.mjs`, platform: "node", target: "node24" });
  await Deno.writeTextFile(`${out}/functions/index.func/.vc-config.json`, JSON.stringify({
    runtime: "nodejs24.x", handler: "index.mjs", launcherType: "Nodejs", supportsResponseStreaming: true,
  }));
  // … copy _fresh/client to static/, write config.json routes
} else if (host === "netlify") {
  await build({ ...common, entryPoints: ["scripts/netlify-edge.mjs"],
    outfile: "netlify/edge-functions/fresh.js", platform: "neutral", external: ["node:*"] });
}

Source: Fresh deployment

methodology.disclaimerHtml: AI-generated note: This document was drafted with AI assistance and checked against vendor documentation. It is a check of capability only: nothing here was measured or benchmarked. Capability is described as of the versions in Versions checked for the nine main-table columns, and the Version line under each framework in Additional frameworks for the six additional frameworks. Setup links point to vendor documentation and were link-checked on 2026-11-24. Claims flagged as uncertain are listed in Lower-confidence claims.
methodology.labelsHtml:
• ✅ 1st-party / built-in — the framework covers it with a default, a stable flag, or an official module/package from the framework team. Whether it is on by default or added as a module does not matter: @nuxt/image, @sveltejs/enhanced-img, and next/image all count the same.
  • 🧪 Experimental / third-party — the only path is a first-party API marked experimental or unstable, or a community package maintained outside the framework team.
  • 🔧 Manual — nothing covers it; the app (or this repo) wires it by hand, or goes without.

🧪 third-party applies when a community package or host service usable with that framework provides the feature itself (not just a building block the app still assembles by hand), whether or not the vendor docs mention it; each such entry names it. Partytown is credited only where the framework's own docs point to it.

The labels describe framework capability, not what a particular port chose. Opt-in is not a penalty. Several ports took a manual or third-party route even where a first-party primitive existed; the feature sections below call that out and link the vendor docs for each framework.

Rubric change: these labels follow a revised rubric (opt-in is no longer penalized; 🔶 and ❌ are removed), so scores are not comparable with earlier versions of this file.

Evidence: Each framework entry links the vendor docs for its label; 🔧 (and 🧪 third-party) entries link the docs page that covers the topic without a first-party primitive (worded "no first-party X documented", not "cannot"). Some labels follow the project owner's rubric decision rather than a literal reading of the linked docs; those cells are listed in Lower-confidence claims.
methodology.scoringHtml:
✅ = 2 points, 🧪 = 1, 🔧 = 0. Each table ends with a score row, which is the sum of its column. To recompute one by hand, read down a column and add:

Next, first table Label Points
Production CSS inlining 🧪 1
Font optimization ✅ 2
Image pipeline ✅ 2
Data/HTML caching ✅ 2
Route prefetching ✅ 2
Total 9

That matches the 9 in the score row. The second table works the same way over seven rows (max 14), and the ranking adds the two totals.
methodology.rankingHtml:
How to read the ranking

Completeness % = (critical-path levers + other features) / 24, rounded to a whole percent. It measures the breadth of first-party and ecosystem performance features, not speed: items are unweighted, rows are not normalized against each other, and the islands row merges partial hydration, server islands, and lazy slices (best label). No measurements are used. Ties share a rank (2, 2, 4) and keep the earlier column order. Scores use the revised rubric and are not comparable with earlier versions.

How to recompute it

  1. Score each cell: ✅ = 2, 🧪 = 1, 🔧 = 0.
  2. Sum each table's column to get the score row (max 10 for the critical-path levers, max 14 for the other features).
  3. Add the two scores for the total (max 24), then divide by 24 for the completeness percentage. For example, Nuxt: 10 + 12 = 22, and 22 / 24 rounds to 92%.

Treat this as a rough capability count only, not a performance prediction.
methodology.otherFeaturesSummaryHtml:
Summary: Nuxt and Pracht tie for the widest set (12 of 14). Nuxt has per-route rules, documented lazy hydration and experimental islands (🧪), modern-format images, first-party reactivity, an experimental analyzer, an official script module, and Nitro presets. Pracht is the only framework where islands are a per-route hydration mode, and it also has server islands, ISG, an analyzer, a script component with loading strategies, and first-party adapters. TanStack Start has per-route SSR control, experimental deferred hydration (🧪), and (React only) experimental Server Components. SvelteKit sits in the middle: strong routing and deploy primitives, but no islands and no built-in script or analysis tooling. SolidStart has the same gaps in script and analysis tooling, but gets modern-format <picture> output from the Solid team's @solidjs/image and experimental server components in Solid 2 (🧪); its deploy targets rely on Nitro and host-maintained plugins (🧪). Waku gets per-route rendering, adapters, and lazy slices, but its React runtime gives it no islands or fine-grained reactivity. Ember has autotracking and only a community analyzer beyond that.

The honest reading is that Next's strength is server rendering, not breadth. It has React Server Components, Cache Components/PPR, and cache tags, which these tables do not try to score. It scores 🔧 on art-direction ergonomics, and 🧪 on deploy adapters and reactivity.
methodology.additionalFrameworksHtml:
Labels for these six frameworks come from vendor documentation and the package registry (npm; JSR for Fresh), at the versions listed under each framework, using the same legend and scoring as above. Ports of all six now exist (astro-books, react-router-books, qwik-books, angular-books, marko-books, fresh-books; see the README for repos and deploys), each with a main baseline and an optimized branch (cache + self-hosted fonts) deployed to Vercel, Netlify, and Cloudflare. The labels below were not derived from those ports.

Why these frameworks: widely used alternatives with an SSR/SSG story. Not included: Gatsby, Eleventy, Remix v2 (superseded by React Router), Analog, RedwoodSDK, and SvelteKit-adjacent projects.
lowerConfidenceClaims: TanStack Start (Solid)'s <Hydrate> guide has prose copied from the React variant, and its runtime behavior was not confirmed by building the Solid port.
TanStack Start (Solid) has no ISR guide; its caching label leans on the React ISR guide and the static-prerendering docs.

The 🧪 third-party labels for the TanStack ports' fonts, images, and analysis, and the 🔧 label for scripts, mean the docs make no first-party mention — not that these cannot be added by hand. The TanStack production checklist only tells readers to inspect fonts, images, and third-party scripts, not to use a primitive.

TanStack Start and SolidStart multi-host deployment (🧪): Nitro is a separate project and the Cloudflare and Netlify Vite plugins are host-maintained, although the TanStack hosting guide and the Solid deployment docs present them as the official setups. Scored ✅ on that basis, as before this revision, each of the three columns would gain 1 point.

The TanStack Start (Solid) doc links are the latest guides, which describe the v1 line (npm latest 1.169.7, Solid 1, vite-plugin-solid); the port runs @tanstack/solid-start 2.0.0-rc.8 on Solid 2 RC with @solidjs/vite-plugin, and tanstack.com publishes no separate v2 docs. The cited APIs (Hydrate, server.build.inlineCss, route ssr and headers, defaultPreload) were confirmed present in the 2.0.0-rc.8 packages, but the guides may not describe that line exactly.
Waku scripts (🔧): the linked migration page does not mention third-party scripts; the label rests on no primitive being documented there.

Ember's 🔧 cells (CSS, scripts) and 🧪 third-party cells (fonts, images via the community @responsive-image/ember, analysis) rest on the absence of a first-party primitive: the Ember Vite guide covers build setup only; the guides' only CSS and asset material is a generic HTML/CSS/JavaScript primer and the tutorial's CSS-and-assets section (app/styles/app.css, public/ for images and fonts); Embroider's Analyzing Bundles page defers to Vite tooling. The older cli.emberjs.com asset-compilation page is deprecated and covers the classic pipeline, so it is not cited.

Cells where the project owner's label differs from what the linked docs show (kept as given): SolidStart data caching 🔧 (Nitro routeRules / defineCachedHandler, nitro.build/docs/cache; Solid Router query); SolidStart per-route render modes ✅ (an app-level Nitro prerender list plus Nitro routeRules; Nitro is not a Solid-team package and there is no per-route SSR/SPA switch); Next and Pracht art direction 🔧 (stable first-party getImageProps() helpers exist; scored 🔧 because neither ships a <picture>-emitting component); Waku data caching ✅ (waku-cache is a separate, still-evolving package, and the migration guide says to add caching explicitly); Ember data caching 🔧 (WarpDrive ships a first-party client request cache, docs). In the Data/HTML caching row, ✅ is given where vendor docs describe build-time prerender or static output plus response cache headers, even with no framework data cache (SvelteKit, TanStack Start, React Router, Qwik City, Angular; Marko on static output alone, see below). SolidStart (prerender, Nitro routeRules) meets that bar and is kept at 🔧 by the project owner; scored by the same bar it would gain 2 points. Fresh stays 🔧 because it documents only a hand-set Cache-Control header.

Nuxt lazy hydration is on by default and documented without a warning on the components page, but its config key is experimental.lazyHydration on the Experimental Features page; the islands cell is 🧪 on that basis, as are experimental server components and <NuxtIsland>.

Nuxt bundle analysis 🧪: the nuxt analyze command is documented as experimental; the build.analyze config option carries no experimental label but, with the Vite builder, relies on the community rollup-plugin-visualizer being installed. If that flag were counted as a stable first-party path the cell would be ✅ and Nuxt's total 23 (96%, tied with Astro at rank 1).

@sveltejs/enhanced-img is 1.0.1 on npm and the svelte.dev images page carries no experimental label, but the package README (npm and GitHub main) still says "This package is experimental. It uses pre-1.0 versioning"; the SvelteKit image-pipeline and <picture> cells (✅) treat that README text as stale. Read literally, both cells would be 🧪 and SvelteKit's total would be 17 (71%).
SolidStart image pipeline and <picture> (✅): @solidjs/image is a Solid-team package (GitHub solidjs/solid-image, npm) but is absent from docs.solidjs.com; the labels rest on the package README.
Next was read against the 16.4.6 docs while the port pins 16.4.0-canary.8; ensureStatic, the unprefixed next analyze, and next analyze export (all v16.4.0) are not in the pinned build.

Additional frameworks have main and optimized ports but are not in the Lighthouse runs yet; every label is from vendor docs under the same rubric, not from the ports. Qwik and Astro rows were judged against the rubric as noted in their bullets.

Marko multi-host deployment (✅): the Cloudflare adapter is announced as official on markojs.com (October 2026 newsletter) but is not yet on the adapters page; the Vercel adapter is a first-party package documented only on npm and in the marko-js/run repo, not on markojs.com.

Marko data/HTML caching (✅) is weak: it rests solely on the app-wide @marko/run-adapter-static export (SSG, no revalidation); Marko Run documents no data cache, ISR or cache-header API. If static export alone is not accepted for this row the cell becomes 🔧 and Marko's first-table score drops from 4 to 2.

Qwik v2 (2.0.0-rc.5) differences are unverified; the Qwik labels use v1 docs. Qwik City 1.20.4 ships no Vercel Node/serverless adapter (vercel-edge only); a cloudflare-workers adapter is documented alongside cloudflare-pages and reuses the same adapter code.
Fresh build-time prerender exists only as an open PR and is not credited.

Fresh multi-host deployment (🔧) is a judgment from the documented hosts, as for Angular: Deno Deploy, deno compile, Docker and Cloudflare Workers (through Cloudflare's own @cloudflare/vite-plugin) are documented, but Node, Vercel and Netlify are not. Counting the Cloudflare page as third-party coverage would make this cell 🧪 and Fresh's second-table score 6.

Angular multi-host portability (🔧) is a judgment: Node is first-party and Netlify and Cloudflare SSR are host-maintained, but no Vercel SSR path is documented, so the cell is scored like Fresh (partial host coverage). If three of four hosts were accepted as 🧪, Angular's total would be 18 (75%). The Angular font-inlining label (✅) is weak because only Google/Adobe CSS inlining is documented.

Angular bundle analysis (🧪): the --stats-json flag, the build size summary and size budgets are first-party and stable; only the module-level viewer (esbuild's analyze page) is external. Pracht is scored ✅ for a first-party size report plus budgets, so if that standard is applied Angular's cell becomes ✅ and its total 18 (75%).

React Router multi-host (🧪) is a judgment: Node, Cloudflare, and AWS adapters are maintained by the React Router team, while Vercel and Netlify are host-maintained; read literally, the rubric could give ✅.
Marko Run is 0.x (0.11.19 on npm; 0.11.17 in the port), pre-1.0.

Ember per-route render modes (🔧): community vite-ember-ssr can prerender a listed set of routes (emberSsg({ routes })), the same mechanism that earns React Router and SolidStart their ✅ when first-party. Credited as a community package it would be 🧪, giving Ember 6 (25%), still last.

React Router naming: "v7" in older material is the same framework mode that docs now call v8 (npm latest 8.5.2); the how-to pages give no minimum versions, but the changelog dates the prerender config to v7.0.0, unstable RSC Data Mode APIs to v7.7.0, and unstable RSC Framework Mode to v7.9.2.
Angular incremental-hydration and route-level render-mode stability (stable since v20) comes from the Angular roadmap, not from the guides.

Also flagged UNSOURCED inline and not affecting any label: Angular's default router preloading strategy (not stated on the fetched page), the behaviour of Astro's security.csp (unscored extra), and whether a Vite ?inline CSS import works in Fresh.
Next worker strategy and Bun adapter status are taken from the linked docs as of this edit; Cloudflare/Netlify verified adapters are described there as in progress.

Pracht was checked on 0.18.0; it has since reached 1.0 (latest 1.0.1), and the linked Pracht docs are unversioned, so they describe the current release rather than the pinned one. Several ports pin pre-release builds: Next (16.4.0-canary.8), Nuxt (4.6.0 nightly on the optimized branches), Waku (1.0.0-rc.0), TanStack Start Solid (2.0.0-rc.8), and the SolidStart pieces (Solid 2 RC, Nitro 3 beta). @tanstack/react-start itself is on stable 1.169.x, but both TanStack ports use a Nitro 3 beta. Vendor docs can change week to week.

SolidStart is not @solidjs/start here: Solid 2 (port pinned to 2.0.0-rc.6; 2.0.3 is npm latest) in @solidjs/vite-plugin start mode plus Nitro 3 beta. SolidStart v2 itself is stable on Solid 1 and its docs are at v1.solidjs.com. The doc links in this file are references, not a description of this port's build. Links to v1.solidjs.com describe released SolidStart v2 / Solid Router v1; links to docs.solidjs.com describe Solid 2 start mode.

No inline example (unsourced) because no repo file or linked doc page supplied one: CSS inlining for Waku and Ember; images for Waku and Ember; prefetching for Ember; islands for SolidStart and Ember; Next islands (prose only; the flag snippet is in section 4); Next and Ember per-route render modes; <picture> for SolidStart, TanStack Start (React and Solid), Pracht, Waku, and Ember; TanStack Start (React) and Pracht reactivity; bundle analysis for SvelteKit, SolidStart, TanStack Start, Waku, and Ember; third-party scripts for SvelteKit, SolidStart, Waku, and Ember; multi-host deployment for Ember. The TanStack Start (Solid) caching, prefetching, scripts, and deployment entries reuse the React snippet instead of repeating it, and its reactivity entry reuses the SolidStart one.
Several snippets are shortened (marked "omitted" or "abridged" in their captions) and some doc snippets are adapted from short quotes.
